title: Persian carpet knotting
summary: A hand-knotted carpet is built one knot at a time: the weaver follows a coloured chart in which every square stands for a single knot of dyed wool. Medallions, borders, garden layouts and leaf-like boteh shapes grow from the middle outward, the same on every side.
howToPlay: Pick a wool colour and a shape from the strip under the chart: solid knots, diamonds, stars, leaves, rings and hexagons.
Tap a square to tie a knot: the knots on the other three sides and the mirrored corners follow, so the chart stays balanced.
Copy the small chart above, then press Check.
rules: The chart is balanced in four turns and in mirror image, as carpet fields are.
A square scores only when its shape and its wool colour both match the chart.
Tying the same shape and colour again, or using the eraser, removes the knot.
Three stars need a near-perfect copy; undo and clear are free.
heritageNote: Carpet weaving has been practised for centuries in towns, villages and tribal camps across Iran and Turkey, each region with its own colours and layouts, and it is still a major household and workshop craft.
